The centre frequency is about 2e7 Hz against a 25–31 Hz target, roughly six orders of magnitude off, while gain, power and DC level pass. The frequency is set by the R·C products in the feedback network, so the fault is most likely in one of the feedback capacitors or resistors. I can't pin it down from these numbers alone. A single element off by one or two orders of magnitude would not produce a 7e5 shift, so this ranking is a best guess, not a confirmed diagnosis.

```json
{"ranking": ["C2", "C1", "R3"], "fault": "Feedback capacitor C2 (a-n, 7.868e-13 F) is likely mis-scaled (units or value error). Its RC product with the feedback network is far too small, pushing f0 to ~2e7 Hz instead of ~28 Hz. The original value should be roughly 10^3-10^6 times larger, consistent with the target. Simulation with a fixed C2 is needed to confirm."}
```
